svg.text: MediAlabat SMS gateway · ESP32 + SIM800L EVB (V2.3)
Wiring & setup · keep everything UNPLUGGED while you connect wires · 2G-only modem: check 2G coverage where it will sit
TX goes to RX and RX to TX, so the green and blue wires cross on purpose
PIN lock OFF · registered · has load
Put it in a phone first: turn the SIM PIN lock OFF, check it is
registered and has load or a text promo. Send yourself a test SMS.
Fit the SIM and the antenna
Micro-SIM into the EVB's slot, antenna onto its connector,
Seat the ESP32 on the breadboard
Straddle the centre groove. On a half-size board the pin
columns get crowded - a full-size one leaves room for wires.
5 signal/ground wires + 2 power wires, exactly as drawn.
TX goes to RX and RX to TX - the green and blue wires cross.
5 V adapter (2 A or more) to the EVB's 5V and GND pins.
Then USB from ESP32 to PC. Never power the EVB from the ESP32.
Test the modem by hand first
Upload the pass-through sketch from the guide and try the AT
commands below. Only continue once they all answer correctly.
Edit Wi-Fi, SERVER_BASE and DEVICE_KEY in the .ino file,
upload it, start MediAlabat as shown below, approve a request.
Arduino Serial Monitor: 115200 baud, line ending "Both NL & CR"

svg.text: No answer to AT? Swap the TXD/RXD wires, check the common ground,
try 115200 baud in the sketch. Resets / no network = weak 5 V supply.
Then send yourself a test text: guide section 4 (docs/ESP32_SMS_GATEWAY.md).

svg.text: ESP32 and PC must be on the same Wi-Fi/network. Give the PC a
fixed IP in your router, allow port 5000 in the firewall, and
Never power the EVB from the ESP32's 3V3 or VIN pins.
VDD takes the ESP32's 3.3 V only - never 5 V.
Use a real 5 V adapter (2 A+) with a short, thick cable -
not a PC USB port. A weak supply makes the modem reset.
Pin names / order can differ between EVB versions: follow
the labels printed on YOUR board before powering it.
Optional: 1000 uF capacitor across the EVB's 5V and GND
2G only: make sure your SIM registers where this will sit.

Drawn from the common blue SIM800L EVB layout (pin order: 5V, GND, VDD, TXD, RXD, GND, RST) and a 30-pin ESP32 DevKit. Exact pin order and labels can differ between sellers and board revisions - match the names printed on your own boards before you apply power.
